subject: How to summarize two different variables for geom_bar

messages.author: e24eaa439804509c
messages.subject: How to summarize two different variables for geom_bar
parts:
Hi All,

I have the following data:

TOPIC, YEAR
A, 2006
A, 2007
B, 2006
B, 2008
...

YEAR ranges from 2006-2010 and some topics occur in some years but not
in others. I want to build a bar chart where the X-axis is the number
of years a topic occurs in (1-5) and the length of the bar is the
number of topics that occur in that many years. So, this is sort of
like summarizing two different variables. I really think I should be
able to do this within ggplot2 (using some combination of 'group' and
'weight') without needing to write additional code to massage this
data. Am I wrong?

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks!

If I read your questions correctly:

This is sudo code, but I think It should do the trick for what your
are after.
The code is pretty much directly from http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html


ggplot(your.data.frame, aes(x=factor(year), fill=TOPIC))+geom_bar()

Sorry about being unclear. TOPIC represents topics that are used for a
task that happens each year. YEAR represents the year (from 2006 to
2010). However, not the same topics are used each year. So, I want to
see how many topics are used only for 1 year out of 2006-2010, how
many are used for 2 of the years and so on.

So, for the example data in my post, X and Y would be 2 and 2 (since A
and B were both used for 2 out of 5 years).

Does that make sense?

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: How to summarize two different variables for geom_bar
parts:
I'm probably making this more complicated than it is, just waiting for
someone to embarrass me by posting a one-liner using xtabs or
something. Anyway, I think you want

dat.plot <- ddply(ddply(dat, .(TOPIC), transform,
n.year = length(unique(YEAR))), .(n.year), summarize,
n.topic = length(unique(TOPIC)))

ggplot(dat.plot, aes(x = n.year, y = n.topic)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity")

And no, I can't think of a way to do that directly in ggplot.

Best,
Ista
